summary:
Participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge with Challenge 3: "Build a Young Astronaut Training Model", our team has developed an interactive trivia game on the Blooket platform. This project plays a crucial role in simplifying academic space knowledge, helping young children develop an early passion for science, and training quick reflexes through a "learn through play" approach.
We researched actual training protocols and translated them into short multiple-choice questions (A, B, C, D) revolving around 6 core topics:
Nutrition & Health: Diet and maintaining physical condition in outer space.
Knowledge & Technology: Astronomical knowledge and spacecraft operation.
Physical Training: Building endurance and adaptability.
Emergency First Aid: Handling unexpected medical situations.
Space Survival: Responding to technical failures, lack of oxygen, and radiation.
Earth-based Missions: Communication skills and executing commands from mission control.
This solution helps "young astronauts" comprehensively improve their physical fitness, intellect, and survival skills, preparing them to conquer space in the future.
details:
1. What does the project do and how does it work? The "Build a Young Astronaut Training Model" project simulates NASA's actual astronaut training process as an online interactive trivia game system on the Blooket platform. Players (children) take on challenges in the form of multiple-choice questions (A, B, C, D) divided into 6 core training modules:

  • Nutrition & Health: Learn about special diets and how to maintain physical condition in a zero-gravity environment.
  • Knowledge & Technology: Grasp basic astronomical knowledge and the operating principles of spacecraft.
  • Physical Training: Build knowledge about endurance and the body's adaptability.
  • Emergency First Aid: Equip skills to handle unexpected medical situations in outer space.
  • Space Survival: Develop a mindset for responding to technical failures, oxygen deprivation, or space radiation.
  • Earth-based Missions: Practice communication skills, coordination, and accurately executing commands from ground control.

2. Benefits and intended impact of the project

  • Benefits: Transforms dry, academic space science knowledge into something relatable, easy to understand, and engaging through gamification ("learning through play"). Helps children develop critical thinking, decision-making skills, and quick reflexes in hypothetical scenarios.
  • Intended impact: Sparks a passion for space exploration and STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) among the younger generation starting from school age, creating a foundation of knowledge and readiness for "future astronauts."

3. Tools and software used

  • Game deployment platform: Blooket (for building interactive question sets and competitive game modes).
  • Design & presentation tools: Google Slides / Canva (for creating presentation materials and illustrating the training model).
  • Reference data sources: Public educational materials and astronaut training protocols from NASA.

4. Creativity and factors considered by the team

  • Creativity: Instead of providing one-way theoretical instruction, the team gamified the entire rigorous training roadmap of a real astronaut into short, highly competitive role-playing stages with instant feedback.
  • Factors considered: The team paid special attention to age-appropriateness (relatable language and short question durations to maintain children's focus), comprehensiveness (balancing physical fitness, intellect, and survival skills), and accessibility (using a free web-based platform that is easy to deploy in classrooms or at home without complex equipment).
